body:
Re-files T-01KYSC1SJ10F7BHCMT0ERFAKM9, which PR #509 annotated `completed: true` while sweeping "42 shipped railless tickets". That sweep matched on a ticket having no rails, which is a statement about privilege rather than about whether the work shipped. This one had not shipped, and still has not: every line it names is unchanged. Re-filed rather than un-completed because `rail-freeze` permits ADDING `completed: true` to a base ticket and nothing else, so removing it needs a maintainer override, while authoring a new ticket needs no ceremony.

=== THE DEFECT, RE-MEASURED ON 86a5e75d ===

`readManifestForest`'s entries array is ordered by anchor topology (anchored-to segment, anchored-to seq, own ULID) for DISPLAY. Its own header comment in `packages/gate-manifest/lib/forest.mjs` states that this is deliberately not a causal or temporal order across independent segments. Three consumers still treat array position as chronology:

  packages/runner/lib/assertions.mjs:45    latestP5Entry  -> .at(-1)
  packages/runner/lib/assertions.mjs:277                  -> .at(-1)
  packages/runner/lib/assertions.mjs:180   entries.slice(0, entries.indexOf(entry))
  packages/runner/lib/assertions.mjs:199   entries.indexOf(entry)
  packages/runner/lib/assertions.mjs:235   entries.slice(index + 1, completionIndex)
  packages/runner/lib/acceptance.mjs:20    latestP5Entry  -> .at(-1)
  packages/prosecute/lib/run.mjs:183       for (const entry of entries) with sequential Map.set/delete

Concretely: when a finding is verified in one segment and killed in a DIFFERENT segment that sorts earlier, these consumers can name the wrong "latest" P5 entry, misjudge whether a finding was killed before completion, or let P5 report clean while a finding is still open. The failure needs a ticket whose P5 evidence spans more than one `manifest.d/` segment, which the segment writer (slice 3, PR #411) made a reachable state.

Originally found by adversarial-review plus 2 of 5 P5 prosecution lenses during slice 3; see PR #411 for the reproduction reasoning.

=== WHAT CHANGED SINCE THE ORIGINAL WAS WRITTEN ===

Nothing in these three files. The forest itself has moved on — the manifest root is frozen and new evidence mints segments under `.adlc/manifest.d/` — which makes multi-segment evidence per ticket the ordinary case rather than an edge one, so the reachability argument is now stronger than when this was first filed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No P5 consumer decides chronology from forest array position. The fix may either scope each read to the root plus this branch's own open segment (the `readOwnChains`/`peekOpenSegment` pattern already used by `packages/tickets/lib/doctor.mjs`, `packages/ticket-sync/lib/reassign.mjs` and `packages/ticket-sync/lib/push.mjs`), or establish a genuine causal order before any position-based comparison. verify: `node --test packages/runner/test/*.test.mjs`
- A finding verified in one segment and killed in a later-written but earlier-SORTING segment is reported as killed, not open. The test builds the two segments explicitly rather than relying on whatever order a live run happens to produce. verify: `node --test packages/prosecute/test/*.test.mjs`
- The same two-segment shape drives `latestP5Entry` to the causally latest entry, in both `assertions.mjs` and `acceptance.mjs`. verify: `node --test packages/runner/test/*.test.mjs`
- The tests bite: each new case fails against the current implementation, asserted against a fixture rather than by inspection. verify: `node --test packages/runner/test/*.test.mjs && node --test packages/prosecute/test/*.test.mjs`
- A single-segment repo keeps its current answers, so this does not change behaviour for a repo that never split. verify: `node --test packages/runner/test/*.test.mjs`
- The three CI gates pass on a freshly fetched base. verify: `npm run preflight`

allow-suppression: none

=== SURFACES THIS LEAVES ALONE ===

`readManifestForest`'s ordering itself is correct for what it is documented to do, and display consumers that want topological order keep it. The change belongs in the consumers that need causality, not in the reader.

Gate-manifest's own `verify()` and the chain-integrity checks are a separate concern from finding lifecycle and are unaffected.
title: P5 gate consumers still read forest array position as chronology
